title: Ahead
hook: a teacher, a sangha, a retreat, a reading list, a vow: the path goes on
tomorrow: what did the Buddha do on the night everything changed?

segments.voice: Yesterday, dedication: the good of five years given away, to the living, the departed, every being. May it be shared. Today, the last night of the Buddha's life, and what he left to go on with.

Between two sala trees at Kusinara, lying on his right side, the Buddha was dying. It was his last night, and the monks had gathered close. The trees, the sutta says, flowered out of season, and the petals drifted down onto his body. Then a wanderer named Subhadda came, asking to see him. Ananda turned him away: the Teacher is weary. Subhadda asked again. Again, no. He asked a third time.
screen: `TWO SALA TREES.` → `PETALS FALLING.` → `A THIRD TIME, ASKING.`

segments.voice: The Buddha heard, and said: let him come. He asks to understand, not to trouble me. Subhadda asks, listens, and becomes the last disciple the Buddha received himself. Then the Buddha turns to Ananda with what comes after. Some of you may think: the word of the teacher is over; we have no teacher now. Don't see it that way. The teaching and the discipline I've given you, after I'm gone, let them be your teacher. He named no one to take his place. Earlier in the same sutta he had told Ananda he never thought of the sangha as depending on him, or of himself as the one who must lead it. The dhamma teaches, and the sangha keeps it alive between people. So the path goes on in ordinary shapes: a teacher who has walked further, a sangha to sit with, a retreat, a shelf of suttas, the precepts taken again as a vow. Then he asked the monks, three times, whether anyone had a doubt left. No one spoke. And his last words, in Rhys Davids' translation: "Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!" The Pali under diligence is appamada: not letting up, staying awake. His last words weren't, it's over. They were, keep going.
screen: `LET HIM COME.` · `THE TEACHING IS YOUR TEACHER.` · `A TEACHER, A SANGHA, A VOW.` · `WORK IT OUT WITH DILIGENCE.` · then, large: `THE PATH GOES ON.`

segments.voice: Stand and take three slow steps, feeling each one: the heel lifting, the foot moving, the foot coming down. Then sit, pick up a pen, and write one step for the year ahead on this path: a teacher to look for, a sangha to visit, a retreat, a book, a vow. One step, in your own hand.
Ahead: the path past the summit, with the dhamma as teacher and diligence, appamada, for the walking.
For the road: the path goes on, one step at a time, with the teaching as your teacher. Twelve of fourteen, done.

screen: `DAY 1789 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 12 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID THE BUDDHA DO ON THE NIGHT EVERYTHING CHANGED?`

howItsDone: After learning the basics, Buddhists often look for a teacher and a sangha to practice with, go on retreats, keep reading the suttas, and take or renew the precepts, sometimes as a formal vow at a temple.

fork.setup: your meditation group's leader moves away, and the group stops sitting until someone can be named the new master. using the Buddha's last night, what fits?
options: keep sitting together with the teaching as teacher; the group keeps it alive.
wait until a successor is named; without a master the teaching can't go on.
split up and sit alone; once the leader leaves, a group has no point.
fork.reveal: the Buddha named no successor. the teaching and the discipline would be the teacher, and the sangha keeps it alive between people.

options: the Buddha said the teaching is the teacher, and a sangha there keeps it alive.
nobody; after the basics, a real Buddhist doesn't need any teachers at all.
you'll need a new master to take over from ông, like a successor.
chat.meaning: On his last night the Buddha named no successor: the teaching and the discipline would be the teacher, kept alive by the sangha.

tie.story: Dying at Kusinara, the Buddha told Ananda the teaching and discipline would be their teacher after him.

notes: DN 16 paraphrased: the twin sala trees bloom out of season and petals fall on the Buddha's body; Subhadda asks three times and Ananda refuses three times; the Buddha overhears and admits him; Subhadda is the last disciple he received personally. Confirm.
DN 16.6.1 paraphrased: 'the dhamma and vinaya I have taught will be your teacher after I am gone'; the Buddha asks three times whether any monk has a doubt, and all are silent. Confirm.
Last words quoted from Rhys Davids 1881 (SBE XI); confirm exact wording. 'The Pali under diligence is appamada' refers to appamadena sampadetha; confirm.
'He named no one to take his place' follows DN 16; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with the framing that Buddhism has no single successor.
Practice: three slow walking steps (senses shape, movement), then the outline practice, write one step for next year. Writing appears twice in seven days (1784, 1789), within the rotation rule.
Shape: senses (petals falling; footsteps). Mai's storyline: after the memorial chanting, ông tells her the dhamma will be her teacher at college; graduation is days away.
Surprising fact: on the night he died, the Buddha still made time for one newcomer, Subhadda, after Ananda had turned him away three times.
